lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Prepare one discussion question about a character's feeling that requires a quotation to answer.

FEEDBACK
Strong question: What shows the character is unsure? Expected answer uses a quoted clue.

CHECK
Yes/no questions with no text link give thin discussion.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Read a short passage aloud, then lead a three-turn discussion with a parent or peer using two evidence-based questions. Record the best quotation used.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Read-aloud and discussion combine expressive reading with talk that uses evidence from the text.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Read a short passage aloud, then lead a three-turn discussion with a parent or peer using two evidence-based questions. Record the best quotation used. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Strong question: What shows the character is unsure? Expected answer uses a quoted clue. Reasoning: I used read-aloud by attending to discussion and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Yes/no questions with no text link give thin discussion. Correction: Strong question: What shows the character is unsure? Expected answer uses a quoted clue. Why: the correction restores accurate use of read-aloud.

Parent: Likely misconception: Yes/no questions with no text link give thin discussion. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating read-aloud on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with read-aloud, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
After reading the fog jetty paragraph aloud with a slower pace on "dusk", we discussed whether the character felt fear, quoting "hands shook".

TRY FIRST
Prepare one discussion question about a character's feeling that requires a quotation to answer.

FEEDBACK
Strong question: What shows the character is unsure? Expected answer uses a quoted clue.
teach_steps.explain:
Read-aloud and discussion combine expressive reading with talk that uses evidence from the text.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Yes/no questions with no text link give thin discussion. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
